Title: Setting off
Summary: During the four years of my PhD I spent a lot of time dreaming of vanlife, and watching a lot of youtube videos for inspiration. On the 13th of July 2019 I bought a Mercedes Sprinter (long wheel base) for £7,000. It had been used as a delivery van previously and had 160k miles on the clock but was in good condition. I converted it into a campervan by cladding the interior with pine, cutting holes in the sides for windows, and putting in beds, a kitchen, electric (solar powered) and storage spaces. I built a composting toilet and fitted some back seats for the children which I picked up from a guy who was taking them out of an old minivan, also for a camper conversion. In October that year we finally set off, planning to travel the whole of Europe — if only we'd known covid was coming!

Photos.Title: Here We Go!
Photos.Summary: After three years dreaming of this moment, and three months kitting out Uncle Vanya, we were finally ready to leave! Here we are in Sheffield just before setting off in October 2019, hoping to get to sunny Spain before the cold weather arrived.

Title: A España
Summary: We drove down to the south coast in one go with a Dover-Calais ferry booked. We were giving a lift to a friend of ours who's parents lived near Düsseldorf so we passed quickly through France, Belgium and The Netherlands, stopping for a few ours at Doel (near Antwerp), an abandoned town covered with street art. After Düsseldorf we headed through Luxembourg and down through France to Andorra.

Photos.Title: Denge Sound Mirrors
Photos.Summary: After a long drive down to the south coast in one go we stopped the night near Denge: our first over-night in Vanya. We had our final taste of British cuisine from a fish'n'chip shop and the next day went to have a look at the Sound Mirrors. These were built during WWI to amplify the sound of approaching German planes and would become redundant with the later invention of radar, a little piece of history and science we'd not heard about before and definitely worth a visit.

Photos.Title: White Cliffs of Dover
Photos.Summary: Leaving Britain! We've been on a lot of ferry journeys and not always in the best weather, but leaving from Dover on a clear, sunny day is fantastic: we watch the white cliffs disappear behind us and crowd the front of the ship waiting for the first sight of France, of the continent.

Photos.Title: Doel, Belgium
Photos.Summary: The village of Doel, an island until the 18th century, has been threatened with demolition since 1965 to make room for an expansion of the port of Antwerp. Plans have been halted indefinitely because a handful of villagers have refused to leave, meaning the village is mostly abandoned and a perfect canvas for street artists. After the ferry journey, and then the drive from Calais, we spent a great afternoon exploring here.

Photos.Title: Wildpark Düsseldorf Grafenberg
Photos.Summary: We stayed with a friend of ours near Düsseldorf for a few days before heading further south and he took us to this wildlife park with dear, boar and many other animals.

Photos.Title: Düsseldorf
Photos.Summary: We have visited Köln and Bochum before but out tick-list of Nordrhein-Westfalen cities was missing Düsseldorf. We had a great time there exploring the city and ended up sat outside a bar at a long table eating German bread with mustard.

Photos.Title: K21
Photos.Summary: We love the K21 art gallery in Düsseldorf, we always love interactive art! On our visit several huge wire nets were suspended from the ceiling with a two-storey drop beneath. Definitely one of the more trilling exhibits we've ever seen and loads of fun.

Photos.Title: Wuppertal
Photos.Summary: Leaving Düsseldorf after a couple of nights we first drove to Wuppertal, famous for its suspended monorail train system which once carried a baby elephant. The elephant apparently fell through the floor of the train into the river, but it was not seriously hurt. Fortunately, the floor held out for us as we rode the train not to get anywhere in particular but just to experience it.

Photos.Title: Neroth
Photos.Summary: Probably one of the strangest towns we've been to in Germany, its claim the fame being its former status as a capital of mousetrap manufacturing. The traps were made mainly by women at home, and most of the men in the town became traveling mousetrap salesmen. The town is full of mousetrap memorials, most notably the mousetrap museum.

Photos.Title: Luxembourg
Photos.Summary: We didn't spend long in Luxembourg but we saw the main sights of the capital city, Luxembourg, then spent the afternoon in the huge municipal park and playground. The children liked the clown-shaped water fountain.

Photos.Title: Metz
Photos.Summary: Finally entering France we found ourselves, after a couple of days, in Metz. The main things I remember are the Centre Pompidou-Metz designed by Shigeru Ban with its undulating roof and —when we were there— life-sized bust of King Kong; and also a local skate park where I fell flat on my back merely walking around — I was in pain for about a week after and it is clear that I should work on being able to walk first before I ever take up skateboarding.

Photos.Title: Musée Cinéma et Miniature, Lyon
Photos.Summary: This is a real gem of Lyon. The museum was started by artist Dan Ohlmann who made miniature scenes to be used in wide-shots in films and houses loads of his amazingly detailed creations. But it also features his huge collection of Hollywood memorabilia: the alien from Alien, the hoverboard from Back to the Future, one of the letters addressed to Harry Potter Under The Stairs, prosthetics from Nutty Professor II: The Klumps (that seminal triumph of film-making), and so much more. We were not expecting it to be as fascinating as it was and were blown away.

Photos.Title: Campfire
Photos.Summary: Our first campfire! Driving up-hill to a scenic spot just outside of Lyon we were only looking for somewhere to park discretely to spend the night, but we the picnic area turned out to have a fireplace: good job we had a saw and axe to chop up some fallen branches. When picturing #Vanlife, this is what I had in mind.

Photos.Title: Palais Idéal
Photos.Summary: I really find it hard to describe this place, it's something which has to be seen to be appreciated. Ferdinand "Facteur" Cheval, a local postman, had a vision of an ideal palace in a dream after tripping on an interestingly shaped rock along his route. He then spent the rest of his entire life collecting more rocks and constructing this palace with inspiration from Indian and European architecture he saw in magazines. There are thousands of quirky figurines, hand-carved messages and staircases throughout.

Photos.Title: Carcassonne
Photos.Summary: We couldn't resist stopping off at Carcassonne, being fans of the board game.

Title: La costa al desierto
Summary: My first view of Spain came with blue skies and sunshine as we headed down the Pyrenees into Catalunya. Just hours after being wrapped up warm for the cold and cloud of Andorra la Vella we were sitting in the sun at a café in Montserrat, and the next day lying on the beach in Badalona. In six weeks we experienced the cities of Valencia, Murcia, Alicante and Almeria, besides many smaller towns; we drank wine and beer, and ate churros, in local cafés; we experienced wild smimming in thermally heated rivers and pools; we saw forrests, mountains, beaches and deserts; we played cowboys in Texas Hollywood, Tabernas; and we had Christmas on a secluded beach near Nerja where we were able to lie in the sun and swim in the sea. What an introduction to the country!

Photos.Title: Monistrol de Montserrat
Photos.Summary: Our first stop in Spain, beautiful blue skies, beautiful mountains: a great introduction. We tried ordering in Spanish for the first time: "Un café por favor" and got back: "Speak Catalan or English, we don't speak Spanish here", so we were also introduced to the politics!

Photos.Title: Beach at Badalona
Photos.Summary: Finally made it to the Mediterranean Coast, albeit a fairly industrial stretch. We just stopped here a few hours to sit on the beach before heading off: since that time we've been to hundreds of hugely varied beaches along the Spanish south coast but the sight of the sea after weeks inland is always magical.

Photos.Title: People Towers at Granollers
Photos.Summary: This Catalonian tradition was our first taste of the spectacular and often dangerous world of Fiesta. Coming from England —where we do trick-or-treat, maybe put out some decorations at Christmas and occasionally hang some bunting round the streets for Gay Pride or a royal jubilee— Spanish Fiesta can be overwhelming. They're regular, intense and often crazy. Building ten-person tall human towers with no safety net and a small child balancing on top is definitely one of the wildest!
